questions.question: About how many Americans had already cast ballots before Election Day?
questions.explanation: About 50 million Americans had already voted, with early voting exceeding 2022 levels in every major Senate battleground.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the transition of Ohio’s Senate seat?
options: Jon Husted unseated Sherrod Brown, Brown became vice president, and JD Vance was appointed
Sherrod Brown unseated Jon Husted, JD Vance became vice president, and Husted was then appointed
Jon Husted became vice president, JD Vance was appointed to replace him, and Sherrod Brown later defeated Vance
JD Vance became vice president, Jon Husted was appointed to replace him, and Sherrod Brown later unseated Husted
questions.explanation: Husted was appointed in 2025 to replace JD Vance after Vance became vice president. Sherrod Brown then defeated Husted to return to the Senate.

questions.question: Which five states gave Democrats the governorship and control of both legislative chambers?
options: Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin
Arizona, Georgia, Iowa, South Carolina, and Wisconsin
Texas, Kansas, Maine, Ohio, and North Carolina
Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Iowa, and Nevada
questions.explanation: Democrats secured full state-government control in Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. Arizona could also join the list depending on an undecided legislative race.

questions.question: Where did the U.S. military secretly carry out airstrikes on the eve of the midterm elections?
questions.explanation: The U.S. struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz after Iranian forces fired at American aircraft near the strait.

questions.question: How many Republican-held Senate seats did Democrats flip to win control of the chamber?
questions.explanation: Democrats flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats: Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina, Ohio, Maine, and North Carolina.

questions.question: What did Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer vow to prevent?
options: Democrats from blocking lower-court and Cabinet nominees
Trump from putting “a right-winger” on the Supreme Court
Samuel Alito from remaining on the Supreme Court after January 3
Thomas Massie from forcing a House impeachment vote
questions.explanation: Schumer vowed to stop Trump from putting “a right-winger” on the Supreme Court and warned that Democrats would block lower-court and Cabinet nominees.

questions.question: Approximately how many election monitors did the Justice Department deploy nationwide?
questions.explanation: The Justice Department deployed about 1,000 monitors to more than 120 jurisdictions across all 50 states, its largest election-monitoring operation ever.

questions.question: Who did Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorse in Michigan’s Senate race?
questions.explanation: Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers after previously promising to support Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who defeated her in the primary.

questions.question: What authority would Democrats gain by taking full control of Congress?
options: The ability to select a Supreme Court justice without a presidential nomination
The power to appoint governors in states won by Republicans
Control of congressional committees and subpoena powers
Control of the Justice Department’s election-monitoring operation
questions.explanation: Control of Congress gives Democrats command of congressional committees and subpoena powers, enabling investigations of Trump and his administration.

questions.question: Who called the Republican midterm losses a “Watergate-level repudiation”?
questions.explanation: Ted Cruz described the losses as a “Watergate-level repudiation,” blaming high costs from Trump’s tariffs and the prolonged Iran war.
